why.text: The challenge requires motion-artefact suppression in wearable ECG during walking, and the researcher co-authored work on motion-artifact suppression in wearable ECG using adaptive filtering fused with simultaneous accelerometer data.
The challenge targets AF detection specifically, and the researcher co-authored work on atrial fibrillation detection from single-lead ECG using RR-interval irregularity and rhythm analysis.
The researcher led HEARTWATCH, a three-year project on remote cardiac monitoring for long-term atrial fibrillation screening.

The company has an annotated dataset and a deployed wearable patch (C999-CH1), and the researcher is open to industrial PhD co-supervision and joint applied research projects with technology companies.

problem.text: Using the company's annotated ECG recordings (C999-CH1), Maja Popović would apply adaptive filtering fused with accelerometer data to suppress motion artefacts and then apply AF detection methods to the cleaned signal.

risks.text: SYN-PUB-09638 covers adaptive filtering and AF detection validated on volunteers performing activities including walking; whether the resulting algorithm fits within the hardware constraints of the company's deployed wearable patch is not confirmed by the records.

The embedded algorithm work covers QRS detection and integer arithmetic on microcontrollers; whether the adaptive filtering method fits within the patch's existing hardware constraints is not confirmed by the records.
